title: Hardware instability incident log - chain-of-bid workstation
machine: Windows 11 laptop, RTX 5090 Laptop GPU 24463 MiB, 63.43 GB RAM, 4.0 GB pagefile
purpose: single consolidated record of every observed crash/interruption and the supporting hardware evidence, for later reporting. NOT a causation claim against any model.

standing_hardware_finding.significance: 0:1:0 is the root port the discrete GPU sits behind. Errors are CORRECTED (recovered by hardware) but occur continuously, including at idle with zero GPU load and with no model process running.
standing_hardware_finding.idle_rate_observed: 48-49 events in a 10-minute window post-reboot at 0% GPU utilisation
standing_hardware_finding.gpu_itself_clean: driver 610.62; ZERO XID / nvlddmkm driver faults in 3 days; no HW thermal slowdown, no HW power brake; idle 41 C; ECC N/A (consumer part)

pattern_analysis.interpretation: Seven interruptions across at least four different workload contexts and six different (or absent) bugcheck codes, three of them with no model running at all. Combined with a continuous idle-time PCIe corrected-error stream and a demonstrably clean GPU driver, the evidence points to a platform/PCIe-level hardware fault rather than to any model or training configuration.
pattern_analysis.explicitly_not_claimed: No individual crash has been attributed to a specific driver or component; that requires minidump analysis which has not been performed. Corrected WHEA errors are by definition recovered and do not by themselves prove they escalated into any of these shutdowns.
pattern_analysis.updated_2026_07_27: 8 incidents. The 21 July and 27 July events share a distinct signature: unclean shutdown, no bugcheck, no dump -- more consistent with abrupt power/hardware loss than a kernel exception. Both struck sustained GPU training. Causation is still not attributed to any model or workload.
pattern_analysis.updated_2026_07_27_late: 10 incidents. THREE unclean shutdowns on 27 July alone (15:06:31, 15:39:25, 15:44:45). The last two produced real kernel bugchecks and minidumps -- 0x135 and 0x1E, both with first parameter 0xC0000005 (access violation) -- which no earlier incident in this series did. One of the three struck an idle machine with no workload. Separately: the two training crashes died at global step 396 and 398 of the same run, within two steps of each other, which is either coincidence or a data-dependent trigger and has not been distinguished. Minidumps now exist and have NOT been analyzed; that is the obvious next diagnostic step and needs a debugger toolchain.
pattern_analysis.updated_2026_07_28: 11 incidents. Three consecutive clean training runs (phi, qwen, gemma -- roughly 8.6 h of sustained GPU load) sat between the 27 July cluster and this one, so the fault is intermittent rather than load-triggered. The newly repeating 0x135 code is the most specific signature yet and, combined with the standing PCIe root-port finding (99.4% of 3,545 WHEA events from port 00:01.0, workload-independent), remains consistent with a marginal platform link rather than anything workload-specific. Three dumps now exist and none has been analyzed; that still needs elevation plus a debugger toolchain.
pattern_analysis.updated_2026_07_28_later: 12 incidents, 4 of them on 27-28 July with kernel bugchecks. Both identified codes have now recurred (0x135 at 9 and 11; 0x1E at 10 and 12), every one with first parameter 0xC0000005 (access violation). Four minidumps are retained and none has been analyzed -- that still requires elevation plus a debugger toolchain, neither available in this environment. The workload distribution across all 12 is now: 6 during training, 4 idle, 1 during evaluation, 1 unknown, which continues to argue against a workload-specific cause and for the standing PCIe root-port finding (99.4% of WHEA events from port 00:01.0, present at idle).
pattern_analysis.updated_2026_07_28_ministral: 13 incidents. Ministral alone has now crashed 3 times across two epochs (epoch-1 at step 834/951, epoch-2 at 128/1902 and 821/1902). That is suggestive but NOT established as model-specific: the same host also crashed during granite training twice, during a gemma evaluation, and four times with nothing running at all. The simpler reading remains the standing PCIe root-port fault, which is workload-independent. Ministral's runs are simply long and it has had more exposure.

operational_consequences.mitigations_in_force: --save-steps recovery checkpointing on every long run (proved its value in incident 7); 1-second telemetry (reports/feasibility/monitor_*.csv); strictly sequential GPU work; no concurrent WSL/VM startup during model load
operational_consequences.recommended_next_step: Investigate the PCIe root port fault before further long GPU runs: GPU seating/riser, PCIe link speed and ASPM settings, chipset and GPU driver, BIOS/EC firmware. Separately, the 4.0 GB pagefile is small for a 63 GB machine and leaves little commit headroom (peak observed 54.34 GB of a 67.43 GB limit).

minidump_analysis_2026_07_27.outcome: NOT ANALYZABLE in this environment. C:\Windows\Minidump requires elevation to read; both direct read and PowerShell Copy-Item were denied. No debugger toolchain is installed (kd.exe, cdb.exe, windbg.exe all absent; Windows Kits Debuggers not present). A real analysis needs an elevated shell plus the Windows SDK Debugging Tools, then `!analyze -v`. No analysis was forced or guessed at.
minidump_analysis_2026_07_27.what_is_known_without_them: both bugchecks carry first parameter 0xC0000005 (access violation); 0x1E is KMODE_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED. Two different codes six minutes apart, one of them on a machine with no workload running.
minidump_analysis_2026_07_27.more_useful_finding_instead: see standing_hardware_finding_2026_07_27 below -- the WHEA telemetry turned out to be more specific than the dumps were likely to be.

standing_hardware_finding_2026_07_27.summary: A single PCI Express Root Port is generating corrected AER errors continuously, at a rate of hundreds per hour, all day, independent of workload.
standing_hardware_finding_2026_07_27.interpretation: 99.4% of errors come from root port 00:01.0, which on this platform is the port the discrete GPU attaches through. Corrected means the link is recovering, but a sustained ~400/hour is a genuinely marginal link, not incidental noise. Note the rate does NOT spike around the crashes (121 in the 20-minute crash window is in line with the hourly baseline), so the crashes are not preceded by an error storm -- the link is simply marginal all the time.
standing_hardware_finding_2026_07_27.why_this_matters_operationally: it is independent of workload, which matches the observation that 4 of 10 incidents happened with nothing running. It also means no amount of training-side mitigation (checkpointing, smaller batches) addresses the cause; it only limits the damage.
suggested_next_steps_not_taken: reseat / inspect the GPU PCIe link if physically possible
check for BIOS/chipset firmware updates addressing PCIe AER on this platform
try forcing the link to a lower PCIe generation in firmware -- a standard mitigation for a marginal high-speed link
if elevation becomes available, run `!analyze -v` on the two retained dumps to confirm or refute a driver-level cause
standing_hardware_finding_2026_07_27.not_claimed: This does not prove the root port caused the bugchecks. It is a strong, specific, workload-independent platform signal that was not previously characterized.
